what: American Water Works is the largest publicly traded water and wastewater utility in the United States. It supplies drinking water and treats wastewater for communities across fourteen states, and buys small municipal systems to grow.
customers: About 14 million people in communities across fourteen states, plus military bases under long-term contracts.
money: water supply and wastewater treatment under state regulation
operating water systems on military bases
moat: Regulated monopolies over water networks, a service with no substitute, where returns are set by state commissions and demand barely changes with the economy.
risks: Debt of about $16 billion against almost no cash
Return on invested capital of about 6% is low by design
Regulators set the returns and can reject requested increases
Analyst targets imply the shares are above fair value
opportunities: Revenue grew about 10% last year with a 37% operating margin
Thousands of small municipal water systems need investment they cannot fund, and it buys them
Water demand is the most recession-proof of any utility service
watch: Acquisitions of municipal systems and rate case outcomes.
